language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

Sound is made of vibrations or waves of air. The higher the frequency of the wave, the higher the pitch of the sound they produce. This means that different objects make different pitches of sound.

The shopkeeper gave me examples of different things and asked me to sort them out according to their pitch of sound. Can you help me, by deciding if the objects belong to the low pitch box or the high pitch box?

Strings, frets and tuning pegs help us to change the pitch of the sound of a guitar. A shorter, thinner or tighter string produces a high pitch. But a longer, thicker, looser string produces a lower pitch.
I never tuned an instrument before. Can you help me, by deciding if I’ll get a low or high pitch when I change something?

The pitch of wind instruments is changed by changing the length of the vibrations in the tube. This happens every time the player changes the fingering: opening the holes shortens the bore, closing them lengthens it.
There are also ways of changing the pitch by changing breath pressure or lip tension.
The shopkeeper gave me manuals to tune up 4 different wind instruments. The problem is that some words are missing there. Could you help me by filling in the gaps and tune up the instruments?

helperSimple.text: Ohh! There are some essential words missing in the tuning manuals. Help Ali fill the gaps.
